data.reasoning: The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files including PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, finding standard AUR packaging practices: source downloaded from official PyPI with a pinned b2sum checksum, built with `uv build`, and installed with `python -m installer`. No suspicious network requests, obfuscated code, or dangerous commands were present. The qwen model's inconclusive verdict resulted solely from API errors (HTTP 400) preventing file-by-file review of .SRCINFO and PKGBUILD, not from security concerns. The qwen model's initial PKGBUILD audit also confirmed no top-level code execution risks. With a pinned checksum preventing source substitution and standard build tooling, there are no indicators of supply-chain compromise.
data.disagreement_analysis: The qwen model experienced API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when attempting to review .SRCINFO and PKGBUILD during the file-by-file audit phase, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The disagreement stems from tool failure rather than differing security assessments of the package content.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .SRCINFO and PKGBUILD due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback models when API requests fail with transient errors like HTTP 400 to prevent coverage gaps
Distinguish between initial PKGBUILD sourcing audit (top-level scope only) and comprehensive file-by-file review in coverage reporting and verdict calculation

When critical files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO) cannot be reviewed due to tool errors, the system should either retry automatically or clearly indicate that the inconclusive verdict is due to tool failure rather than security uncertainty
